a1.label: 1. The user's problem was that she...
a1.why: The text says the user could not open any files on the shared drive.

a2.label: 2. First-level support asked her to...
a2.why: The text says first-level support asked her to restart her computer.

a3.label: 3. The cause of the problem was...
a3.why: The text says her permissions had been changed during the system update.

a4.label: 4. As a workaround, Tom...
a4.why: The text says Tom gave her temporary access to a copy of the files.

a5.label: 5. The ticket was resolved...
a5.why: The text says the ticket was closed within the SLA of four hours.

a6.label: 6. The follow-up task is to check...
a6.why: The text says second-level support will check whether other accounts were affected.

b1.label: 1. Every support request is documented in a ___
b1.why: Every support request is documented in a ticket.

b2.label: 2. If first-level support can't solve it, an ___ follows
b2.why: An escalation to second level follows if first-level support can't solve a problem.

b3.label: 3. Defines how quickly a ticket must be resolved
b3.why: The SLA (Service Level Agreement) defines how quickly a ticket must be resolved.

b4.label: 4. A temporary solution that lets the user keep working
b4.why: A workaround is a temporary solution that lets the user keep working.

b5.label: 5. Answers calls and solves simple problems
b5.why: First-level support answers calls and solves simple, common problems.

b6.label: 6. An unplanned interruption to a service
b6.why: An unplanned interruption to a service is called an incident.

b7.label: 7. The ticket stays open until the ___ is confirmed
b7.why: The ticket stays open until the resolution is confirmed by the user.

c1.label: 1. Could you ___ the issue?
c1.why: ‘Could you’ is followed by the base verb.

c2.label: 2. Would you mind ___ your computer?
c2.why: ‘Would you mind’ is followed by the gerund (-ing) form.

c3.label: 3. She said that she ___ not open the files

c4.label: 4. Do you know ___ the error first appeared?
c4.why: Indirect questions keep normal word order after the question word.

c5.label: 5. She told us the error message ___ every time
c5.why: Reported speech backshifts the present simple to the past simple.

c6.label: 6. Could you tell me ___ you have restarted the PC?

c7.label: 7. I was wondering ___ you could give me access
c7.why: ‘I was wondering if’ is the standard polite request pattern.
